title: Python Packages, Project Structure, and Type Hints

questions.question: What can other Python code import as one name?
options: Only a file whose name is main.py
Any directory, as soon as it contains a .py file
A directory of modules that contains __init__.py
A function, but only after the script has already run
questions.explanation: A package is a directory marked by __init__.py. One module is a single file. A directory with no __init__.py is not imported as that package.

questions.question: Which import should a caller outside auditlib use?
options: from auditlib import summarize
from auditlib.load import _row_to_record
from auditlib.stats import open
import auditlib.main as summarize
questions.explanation: summarize is one of the four names __init__.py exports. Helpers that start with an underscore stay in their module. main.py is not part of the package.

questions.question: A test wants the mean score of two reviews. What should it pass to summarize?
options: The path of a CSV that the test just wrote
An open text file positioned at the first row
The string name of the auditlib package
A list of Record values built in the test
questions.explanation: summarize accepts records and does not open files. The loader is the function that accepts a path. The test can build the list in memory.

questions.question: What does import main do when main.py ends with the __name__ guard?
options: It runs main() and prints the sample summary
It loads the module and does not call main()
It refuses to import a file named main.py
It runs main() only when a CSV path is missing
questions.explanation: On import, __name__ is the module name, not __main__. The guard calls main() only when you execute the file.

questions.question: load_records reads a CSV that has the header and no data rows. What does it return?
options: None, because an empty summary is not valid
A Summary with mean_score 0.0
An empty list that the caller can summarize
ValueError, because the file has no records
questions.explanation: A header with no rows is an empty dataset, so the loader returns []. summarize([]) then reports count 0 and mean_score None. A file with no header is the case that raises ValueError.

questions.question: Row 4 has score high, and the header is row 1. Which error is appropriate?
options: ValueError that mentions line 4
FileNotFoundError for the reviews file
A bare except that prints the whole row
Summary with mean_score left as None
questions.explanation: A non-numeric score is invalid input on a known line. FileNotFoundError is for a missing path. The loader raises ValueError before summarize runs.
